# Next.js Engineering Rules

> Rule severity follows RFC 2119. **MUST** rules block merges; **SHOULD** rules require a documented exception in the PR.
> Baseline: Next.js 16 with Turbopack (default bundler). Rules marked **[v15-compat]** apply only to projects not yet migrated.

## App Router & Project Structure

- The App Router (`app/`) MUST be used exclusively. Mixing App Router and Pages Router in one project is forbidden.
- Routes MUST be organized by feature domain under `app/`, using `(group)` route groups for organization. Deeply nested catch-all segments SHOULD be avoided.
- Route-specific components, hooks, and utilities MUST be colocated inside the route segment directory. Promote to a shared location only when two or more routes consume the module.
- The root layout MUST be `app/layout.tsx`. Layout-level UI MUST live in explicit `layout.tsx` files, never inside `page.tsx`.
- Every route segment performing async data access MUST define `loading.tsx` (streaming Suspense boundary) and `error.tsx` (error boundary). `not-found.tsx` MUST be used for explicit 404 UI on routes with unmatchable params.
- `next.config.ts` (TypeScript) SHOULD be used over `next.config.js`.

## Server Components vs. Client Components

- React Server Components are the default. `"use client"` MUST be added only when the module requires browser APIs, event handlers, or client-side state — and pushed to the leaf component that actually needs it, never hoisted to a parent for convenience.
- Server-only modules (database clients, secret readers, fs access) MUST NOT be importable from Client Components. Enforce with the `server-only` package; mark client-only modules with `client-only`.
- Only serializable props may cross the server→client boundary. Functions, class instances, `Map`, `Set`, and other non-serializable objects MUST NOT be passed as props from Server Components to Client Components. Functions that must be invoked client-side MUST be Server Actions (`"use server"`).
- Request context MUST be accessed via `next/headers` inside Server Components, Server Actions, or Route Handlers only. `cookies()`, `headers()`, `draftMode()`, and the `params`/`searchParams` props are async — they MUST be awaited (sync access is removed in v16).

## Data Fetching

- Data MUST be fetched at the Server Component level closest to where it is rendered; do not prop-drill fetched data through layers. Rely on per-render `fetch` deduplication and `React.cache()` for non-fetch data sources instead of re-fetching.
- `useEffect` MUST NOT be used for initial data loading that can occur on the server.
- Caching intent MUST be explicit. Under the v16 Cache Components model (`cacheComponents: true`), everything renders dynamically by default; opt into caching with the `"use cache"` directive plus `cacheLife()` profiles and `cacheTag()` for invalidation. **[v15-compat]** tag every `fetch` with explicit `cache:` or `next: { revalidate }` options; never assume defaults.
- `unstable_cache` is deprecated — new code MUST use `"use cache"`; existing usage SHOULD be migrated via the official codemod.
- Mutations MUST use Server Actions. Do not create API routes solely for form submissions or button-triggered mutations from the same application.
- After a mutation, invalidate precisely: `revalidateTag()` for stale-while-revalidate semantics, `updateTag()` (Server Actions) for read-your-own-writes, `refresh()` for refreshing dynamic data without touching caches.
- All Server Action inputs MUST be validated with a schema (e.g., Zod) before processing. Server Actions are public HTTP endpoints; treat all input as untrusted, and re-check authorization inside every action.
- Every exported Server Action is a callable public endpoint even if no UI references it. Unused actions MUST be deleted, and action modules SHOULD export only what is used.

## Route Handlers & API Layer

- Route Handlers in `app/api/` are reserved for endpoints consumed by external clients, third-party webhooks, or mobile apps. Internal data needs are served by Server Components and Server Actions.
- Export only the HTTP methods the route supports — no catch-all handlers switching on `request.method`.
- Responses MUST be typed `NextResponse`/`Response` objects with explicit status codes.
- Every Route Handler MUST authenticate and authorize at the entry point before reading the request body. Webhook handlers (e.g., CMS revalidation hooks) MUST verify a shared secret or signature before acting.

## Rendering Strategy & Caching

- Content that does not vary per request MUST be prerendered. Use `generateStaticParams` to pre-render known dynamic segments at build time.
- Use cache lifetimes (`cacheLife` profiles, or `revalidate` in v15-compat) based on acceptable content staleness, not convenience. Pair with on-demand invalidation (`revalidateTag`/`updateTag`) triggered by upstream webhooks (e.g., CMS publish events) so staleness windows can be long.
- Dynamic rendering MUST be reserved for genuinely personalized or request-specific content. Do not opt an entire layout/page into dynamic rendering to avoid configuring caching — isolate the dynamic part behind `<Suspense>` and let Partial Prerendering serve the static shell.
- Expensive server-side computations SHOULD be cached with `"use cache"` + `cacheTag` for targeted invalidation.

## Metadata & SEO

- Every `page.tsx` and `layout.tsx` MUST export `metadata` or `generateMetadata`. Title and description are never undefined.
- Dynamic routes MUST use `generateMetadata` with fetched data; hardcoded metadata on dynamic pages is forbidden.
- Canonical URLs MUST be set via `alternates.canonical` in metadata — not delegated to CDN or proxy headers.
- Open Graph images for dynamic content MUST be generated via `next/og` / `opengraph-image` conventions; static OG images are acceptable only for static pages.

## Image & Font Optimization

- All raster images MUST use `next/image`. Raw `<img>` is permitted only for inline SVGs or cases where `next/image` is inapplicable, with a code comment explaining why.
- Every `next/image` MUST define `sizes` matching its CSS layout width; omitting `sizes` makes browsers request the largest variant.
- `priority` MUST be applied only to above-the-fold images critical to LCP — never broadly.
- All web fonts MUST load via `next/font` (self-hosted, subset). `<link rel="stylesheet">` font loading is forbidden — it defeats display optimization and causes layout shift.

## Request Interception (proxy.ts)

- `middleware.ts` is replaced by `proxy.ts` in v16, running on the Node.js runtime. New projects MUST use `proxy.ts`; existing projects SHOULD migrate (rename file, rename export to `proxy`). **[v15-compat]** `middleware.ts` rules below apply equivalently.
- `proxy.ts` MUST be limited to network-boundary concerns: redirects, rewrites, header injection, A/B routing, geolocation, coarse session checks (e.g., "has session cookie → else redirect to /login").
- `proxy.ts` MUST NOT contain database queries or heavy computation, and MUST use the `matcher` config to skip static assets and routes that handle their own auth.
- `proxy.ts` is a routing convenience, NOT a security layer. Authorization MUST be enforced inside Route Handlers, Server Actions, and the data-access layer regardless of any proxy checks. (CVE-2025-29927 — middleware auth bypass via spoofed `x-middleware-subrequest` header — is the canonical lesson: defense in depth is mandatory.)

## Performance & Bundle Management

- The client bundle MUST be analyzed (`@next/bundle-analyzer`) before every major release; no new client-bundle dependency lands without an explicit size review against the route's JS budget.
- Heavy Client Components not needed on initial render MUST be loaded with `next/dynamic` (with `{ ssr: false }` where appropriate).
- Large libraries MUST NOT be imported wholesale (`lodash`, `moment`); import specific functions or use lighter alternatives (`date-fns`, native `Intl`).
- Barrel files with wildcard re-exports are forbidden in application code — they defeat tree-shaking. Exports MUST be explicit.
- React Compiler MAY be enabled (stable in v16) to remove manual memoization; do not hand-write `useMemo`/`useCallback` micro-optimizations that the compiler handles.

## Error Handling & Observability

- Server Components, Server Actions, and Route Handlers MUST emit structured error logs including route, non-PII user context, and a correlation ID.
- `error.tsx` boundaries MUST render actionable recovery UI. Raw error messages, stack traces, and digest internals MUST never reach the client.
- Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) MUST be tracked via `useReportWebVitals` or an observability integration; CWV regressions beyond budget block release (budgets defined in jamstack-rules).
- OpenTelemetry instrumentation (`instrumentation.ts`) SHOULD be used for tracing server-side work in production apps.

## Security

- All security headers required by jamstack-rules MUST be configured in `next.config.ts` `headers()`. For nonce-based CSP, set headers per-request in `proxy.ts` instead of `next.config.ts`. Do not rely solely on hosting-platform defaults.
- Secret environment variables MUST never reach the client. Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_`-prefixed variables are client-safe; all others are server-only. Validate env at boot with a schema.
- All user input in Server Actions and Route Handlers MUST be validated with allow-list schemas before use; deny-list sanitization alone is forbidden.
- Server Actions: restrict cross-origin invocation with `serverActions.allowedOrigins` when running behind proxies/multiple domains. Be aware that values closed over by inline actions are encrypted and sent to the client — never close over secrets; read them inside the action instead.
- Authentication tokens MUST live in `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite` cookies. Custom Route Handlers that accept cookie-authenticated requests MUST implement CSRF protection (double-submit cookie, synchronizer token, or custom request-header check). For Server Actions, confirm `serverActions.allowedOrigins` is correctly scoped and that the running framework version has no unpatched origin-check bypass.
- Next.js and React versions MUST be kept within the supported LTS window; framework security advisories MUST be triaged within one business day.
